key_insight: PING combines graph neural networks with advection–diffusion physics to forecast transport dynamics on irregular sensor networks and support solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Better intra-day photovoltaic power forecasts can support grid integration by combining ground-sensor measurements with satellite cloud information.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on a graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with photovoltaic power forecasting models using ground-sensor and satellite data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models across synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, and improved intra-day photovoltaic forecasting through hybrid modeling.
watch_item: A soft physics constraint guides predictions but does not guarantee physical consistency; the abstract provides no quantitative forecast gains.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
